pages.name: Turn and stretch
pages.text: Multiplying by `w` turns and stretches. Here the arrow 1, 1 long at 0°, turns through 40° and grows 3 times as long, which makes `w = 3∠40°`.

pages.alt: The complex plane, real across and j up. An arc of 30 degrees. An arc of 30 degrees. An arrow from 0: 1. An arrow from 0: z. The arrow 1 at an angle of 0 degrees turns through 40 degrees and its length becomes 3: w. The arrow 2 at an angle of 30 degrees turns through 40 degrees and its length becomes 6: z times w equals 6 at an angle of 70 degrees. Lengths: 2 times 3: 6. Angles: 30 degrees plus 40 degrees: 70 degrees.

pages.why: Multiplying by `2∠50°` turns `4∠25°` through 50° and stretches it 2 times. Its arc is 25° with 50° laid on the end, `25° + 50° = 75°`, and its length is `4 × 2 = 8`. So the answer is `8∠75°`.

pages.name: Times j
pages.text: `j` is `1∠90°`, 1 long at a quarter turn. Multiplying by j adds 90° and multiplies the length by 1, which is no stretch at all.

pages.name: 5∠20° × j
pages.why: `j` is `1∠90°`. Multiplying by it multiplies the length by 1, so 5 stays 5, and adds 90°, so 20° becomes `20° + 90° = 110°`. The answer is `5∠110°`, the arrow turned a quarter turn anticlockwise.

pages.name: Dividing
pages.text: Dividing asks which number, multiplied by w, gives z. Multiplying adds w's angle and multiplies by w's length, so dividing does the opposite.

pages.why: Divide the lengths, `12 ÷ 4 = 3`, and take the bottom's angle from the top's, `80° − 30° = 50°`. So the answer is `3∠50°`. Check by multiplying back: `3∠50° × 4∠30° = 12∠80°`.

pages.task: Work out `4∠120° × 3∠100°`, with the angle in the usual range.
pages.why: Multiply the lengths, `4 × 3 = 12`, and add the angles, `120° + 100° = 220°`. That is past half a turn, so take a whole turn away, `220° − 360° = −140°`. The arrow does not move, so the answer is `12∠−140°`.

pages.name: 10 ÷ (3 + j4)
pages.task: Work out `10 ÷ (3 + j4)` in polar form. `3 + j4` is `5∠53.13°`.
pages.why: `10` is `10∠0°`, and `3 + j4` is `5∠53.13°`. Divide the lengths, `10 ÷ 5 = 2`, and take the angles away, `0° − 53.13° = −53.13°`. So the answer is `2∠−53.13°`. Its parts are `2 cos(−53.13°) = 1.2` across and `2 sin(−53.13°) = −1.6` up, so it is `1.2 − j1.6`, as the conjugate lesson found.

pages.name: Adding is different
pages.text: Multiplying the lengths and adding the angles is the rule for multiplying, not for adding. To add, go back to parts and lay the arrows tip to tail.

pages.name: j2 × j2
pages.why: Multiply the lengths, `2 × 2 = 4`, and add the angles, `90° + 90° = 180°`. `4∠180°` points straight left, so it is `−4`. By parts, `j2 × j2 = j × j × 4 = −4`, the same.
